title: Sumantra Rails at Kaikeyi
introduction: Minister Sumantra requests and reproaches Queen Kaikeyi and asks her to take back her impositions. Even the elderly minister and a scholar named Siddhartha tries to pacify Kaikeyi by telling the legend of Sagara, the ancestor of Dasharatha, quoting the exile of his notorious son Asamanja. But she is adamant to all holy advices, but wants Rama to go to forests.
closing: इति वाल्मीकि रामायणे आदि काव्ये अयोध्य काण्डे पंच त्रिंशः सर्गः

Thus completes 35th chapter in Ayodhya Kanda of the glorious Ramayana of Valmiki, the work of a sage and the oldest epic. verses.devanagari:
ततो निर्धूय सहसा शिरो निःश्वस्व चासकृत् |
पाणौ पाणिम् विनिष्पिष्य दन्तान् कटकटाय्य च
लोचने कोपसम्रक्ते वर्णम् पूर्वोचितम् जहत् |
कोपाभिभूतः सहसा सम्तापमशुभम् गतः
मनः समीक्षमाणश्च सूतो दशरथस्य सः |
कम्पयन्निव कैकेय्या हृदयम् वाक्छरैश्शितैः
वाक्यवज्रैरनुपमैर्निर्भिन्दन्निव चाशुगैः |
कैकेय्या सर्वमर्माणि सुमन्त्रः प्रत्यभाषत
verses.iast:
tato nirdhūya sahasā śiro niḥśvasva cāsakṛt |
pāṇau pāṇim viniśhpiśhya dantān kaṭakaṭāyya ca
locane kopasamrakte varṇam pūrvocitam jahat |
kopābhibhūtaḥ sahasā samtāpamaśubham gataḥ
manaḥ samīkśamāṇaśca sūto daśarathasya saḥ |
kampayanniva kaikeyyā hṛdayam vākcharaiśśitaiḥ
vākyavajrairanupamairnirbhindanniva cāśugaiḥ |
kaikeyyā sarvamarmāṇi sumantraḥ pratyabhāśhata
verses.translation: Then, moving his head all of a sudden sighing again and again, rubbing his hand in hand, grinding his teeth, turning his eyes red with anger shedding his normal colour, overwhelmed with wrath, suddenly getting the evil grief, carefully reading Dasaratha's mind, sumantra the charioteer spoke(as follows) as though shaking Kaikeyi's heart with sharp arrows, in the form of thunderbolting words speedily peircing all her vitals.

glosses.meaning: turning his eyes red with anger
in the form of thunderbolting words

verses.devanagari:
यश्यास्तव पतिस्त्यक्तोराजा दशरथः स्वयम् |
भर्ता सर्वस्य जगतः स्थावरस्य चरश्य च
न ह्यकार्यतमम् किंचित् तव देवीह विद्यते |
verses.iast:
yaśyāstava patistyaktorājā daśarathaḥ svayam |
bhartā sarvasya jagataḥ sthāvarasya caraśya ca
na hyakāryatamam kiṃcit tava devīha vidyate |
verses.translation: "There is nothing on earth, anything which is most disgraceful for you by whom your husband king Dasaratha the supporter of the entire creation the unmoving and the moving, is betrayed, Oh, Kaikeyi!"

verses.devanagari:
पतिघ्नीम् त्वामहम् मन्ये कुलघ्नीमपि चान्ततः
यन्म हेंद्रमिवाजय्यम् दुष्प्रकम्प्यमिवाचलम् |
महोदधिमिवाक्षोभ्यम् सन्तापयसि कर्मभिः
verses.iast:
patighnīm tvāmaham manye kulaghnīmapi cāntataḥ
yanma heṃdramivājayyam duśhprakampyamivācalam |
mahodadhimivākśobhyam santāpayasi karmabhiḥ
verses.translation: "King Dasaratha is unconquerable as great Indra, unshakable as mountain and imperturbable as a great ocean. By tormenting him with your actions, you are considered by me as murderess of your husband and ultimately the exterminator of your race too."

glosses.meaning: the exterminator of your race too
you are causing grief(to your husband) ajayyam = who is unconquerable

verses.devanagari:
मावमंस्था दशरथम् भर्तारम् वरदम् पतिम् |
भर्तुरिच्छा हि नारीणाम्पुत्रकोट्या विशिष्यते
verses.iast:
māvamaṃsthā daśaratham bhartāram varadam patim |
bharturicchā hi nārīṇāmputrakoṭyā viśiśhyate
verses.translation: "Do not despise Dasaratha the supporter, the bestower of boons and your husband. For women, will of the husband is superior to that of ten million sons."

verses.devanagari:
यथावयो हि राज्यानि प्राप्नुवन्ति नृपक्षये |
इक्ष्वाकुकुलनाथेऽस्मिंस्तल्लोपयितुमिच्छसि
verses.iast:
yathāvayo hi rājyāni prāpnuvanti nṛpakśaye |
ikśvākukulanāthe'smiṃstallopayitumicchasi
verses.translation: "After death of a king, kingdoms are obtained as per the age of the princes. But, you want to deprive this condition in the case of Rama the lord of Ikshvaku dynasty."

glosses.meaning: after the death of a king
as per the age(of princes) ichchhasi = you want

verses.devanagari:
राजा भवतु ते पुत्रो भरतश्शास्तु मेदिनीम् |
वयम् तत्र गमिष्यामो रामो यत्र गमिष्यति
verses.iast:
rājā bhavatu te putro bharataśśāstu medinīm |
vayam tatra gamiśhyāmo rāmo yatra gamiśhyati
verses.translation: "Let your son Bharata become the king and rule the earth. wherever Rama goes, we (on our part) shall go there".

verses.devanagari:
न हि ते विषये कश्चिद्ब्राह्मणो वस्तुमर्हति |
तादृशम् त्वममर्यादमद्य कर्म चिकीर्षसि
verses.iast:
na hi te viśhaye kaścidbrāhmaṇo vastumarhati |
tādṛśam tvamamaryādamadya karma cikīrśhasi
verses.translation: "Now any brahmana cannot indeed dwell in your kigdom as now you want to do such an act, transgressing the due limits."

verses.devanagari:
नूनम् सर्वे गमिष्यामो मार्गम् रामनिषेवितम् |
त्यक्ताया बान्धवैः सर्वैर्ब्राह्मणैः साधुभिः सदा
का प्रीती राज्यलाभेन तव देवि भविष्यति |
तादृशम् त्वममर्यादम् कर्म कर्तुम् चिकीर्षसि
verses.iast:
nūnam sarve gamiśhyāmo mārgam rāmaniśhevitam |
tyaktāyā bāndhavaiḥ sarvairbrāhmaṇaiḥ sādhubhiḥ sadā
kā prītī rājyalābhena tava devi bhaviśhyati |
tādṛśam tvamamaryādam karma kartum cikīrśhasi
verses.translation: "Certainly, all of us will proceed in the path followed by Rama. Oh, queen Kaikeyi! What pleasure will be derived through attainment of soverignity, when your relatives, all brahmanas and pious souls desert you forever? Now, you want to do such an act of impropriety"

glosses.meaning: Oh queen Kaikeyi! yaa = which you

verses.devanagari:
आश्चर्यमिव पश्यामि यस्यास्ते वृत्तमीदृशम् |
आचरन्त्या न विदृता सद्यो भवति मेदिनी
verses.iast:
āścaryamiva paśyāmi yasyāste vṛttamīdṛśam |
ācarantyā na vidṛtā sadyo bhavati medinī
verses.translation: "I am looking only with surprise, why the earth is not immediately rent asunder, while you conduct yourself with such an act"

verses.devanagari:
महाब्रह्मर्षिसृष्टा वा ज्वलन्तो भीमदर्शना |
धिग्वाग्दण्डणा न हिंसन्ति रामप्रव्राजने स्थिताम्
verses.iast:
mahābrahmarśhisṛśhṭā vā jvalanto bhīmadarśanā |
dhigvāgdaṇḍaṇā na hiṃsanti rāmapravrājane sthitām
verses.translation: "It is also surprising me why rods of reproaching words fiery and fearful to look at uttered by great brahmana sages are not killing you, who are bent on sending Rama to exile."

verses.devanagari:
आम्रम् चित्वा कुठारेन निम्बम् परिचरेत्तु यः |
यश्चेनम् पयसा सिञ्चेन्नैवास्य मधुरो भवेत्
verses.iast:
āmram citvā kuṭhārena nimbam paricarettu yaḥ |
yaścenam payasā siJṇcennaivāsya madhuro bhavet
verses.translation: "Who will nurture a neem tree, cutting down a mango tree with an axe? And a neem tree will not turn sweet for him who nourishes it with milk."

verses.devanagari:
अभिजात्यम् हि ते मन्ये यथा मातुस्तथैव च |
न हि निम्बात्स्रवेत्क्षौद्रम् लोके निगदितम् वचः
verses.iast:
abhijātyam hi te manye yathā mātustathaiva ca |
na hi nimbātsravetkśaudram loke nigaditam vacaḥ
verses.translation: "I think, by birth your nature is as exactly as that of your mother. a proverb is quoted in the world saying that honey does not ooze from a neem tree."

verses.devanagari:
तव मातुरसद्ग्राहम् विद्मः पूर्वम् यथाश्रुतम् |
पितुस्ते वरदः कश्चिद्ददौ वरमनुत्तमम्
सर्वभूतरुतम् तस्मात्सम्जज्ञे वसुधाधिपः |
तेन तिर्यग्गतानाम् च भूतानाम् विदितम् वचः
verses.iast:
tava māturasadgrāham vidmaḥ pūrvam yathāśrutam |
pituste varadaḥ kaściddadau varamanuttamam
sarvabhūtarutam tasmātsamjajJṇe vasudhādhipaḥ |
tena tiryaggatānām ca bhūtānām viditam vacaḥ
verses.translation: "We know, as heard of in the past, your mother's conduct of evil satisfaction. Someone capable of giving boons, granted a great boon to your father. By that boon he could identify the language of all created beings. The talk of those beings belonging to sub human species could be known by him."

glosses.meaning: the language of all created beings
the talk bhuutaanaam = of those beings

verses.devanagari:
ततो जृम्भस्य शयने विरुताद्भूरिवर्चसा |
पितुस्ते विदितो भावः स तत्र बहुधाऽहसत्
verses.iast:
tato jṛmbhasya śayane virutādbhūrivarcasā |
pituste vidito bhāvaḥ sa tatra bahudhā'hasat
verses.translation: "From the sound of an ant called Jrimbha near his bed, the meaning of that sound was deciphered by your exceedingly brilliant father and he laughed over it repeatedly."

verses.devanagari:
तत्र ते जननी क्रुद्धा मृत्युपाशमभीप्सती |
हासम् ते नृपते सौम्य जिज्ञासामीति भाब्रवीत्
verses.iast:
tatra te jananī kruddhā mṛtyupāśamabhīpsatī |
hāsam te nṛpate saumya jijJṇāsāmīti bhābravīt
verses.translation: Your mother, becoming angry over his laugh, wishing even to hand him to death(in case he refuses to disclose the reason for his laughter), spoke thus: "Oh king, the gentle sir! I want to know the meaning of your laughter."

glosses.meaning: the gentle sir! jiJNaasaami = I want to know

verses.devanagari:
नृपश्चोवाच ताम् देवीम् देवि शंसामि ते यदि |
ततो मे मरणम् सद्यो भविष्यति न संशयः
verses.iast:
nṛpaścovāca tām devīm devi śaṃsāmi te yadi |
tato me maraṇam sadyo bhaviśhyati na saṃśayaḥ
verses.translation: "The king replied to that queen as follows: "Oh, royal lady! If I tell you the reason of my laughter, my death will immediately follow thereafter. There is no doubt about it."

glosses.meaning: to that queen(as follows): devi = Oh

verses.devanagari:
माता ते पितरम् देवि ततह् केकयमब्रवीत् |
शंस मे जीव वा मा वा न मामपहसिष्यसि
verses.iast:
mātā te pitaram devi tatah kekayamabravīt |
śaṃsa me jīva vā mā vā na māmapahasiśhyasi
verses.translation: "Your mother then said to your father, the king of Kekayas, Live or die as you will. tell me the laughter. Do not ridicule me."

verses.devanagari:
प्रियया च तथोक्तः सन् केकयः पृथीवीपतिः |
तस्मै तम् वरदायार्थम् कथयामास तत्त्वतः
verses.iast:
priyayā ca tathoktaḥ san kekayaḥ pṛthīvīpatiḥ |
tasmai tam varadāyārtham kathayāmāsa tattvataḥ
verses.translation: Having been spoken thus by his beloved consort, the said king of the Kekayas on his part correctly reported the matter to the sage who had bestowed the boon on him.

verses.devanagari:
ततः स वरदह् साधु राजानम् प्रत्यभाषत |
म्रियताम् ध्वंसताम् वेयम् मा कृथास्त्वम् महीपते
verses.iast:
tataḥ sa varadah sādhu rājānam pratyabhāśhata |
mriyatām dhvaṃsatām veyam mā kṛthāstvam mahīpate
verses.translation: Then the sage who had bestowed the boon replied to the king as follows: "Oh, lord of the earth! Let her die or ruin. Do not reveal the reason to her."

verses.devanagari:
स तच्छ्रुत्वा वचस्तस्य प्रसन्नमनसो नृपः |
मातरम् ते निरस्याशु विजहार कुबेरवत्
verses.iast:
sa tacchrutvā vacastasya prasannamanaso nṛpaḥ |
mātaram te nirasyāśu vijahāra kuberavat
verses.translation: "Having heard the words of that sage who was pure-minded, the king repudiated your mother and lived happily like Kubera the Lord of riches."

verses.devanagari:
तथा त्वमपि राजानम् दुर्जनाचरिते पथि |
असद्ग्राहमिमम् मोहात्कुरुषे पापदर्शिनि
verses.iast:
tathā tvamapi rājānam durjanācarite pathi |
asadgrāhamimam mohātkuruśhe pāpadarśini
verses.translation: "Oh, Kaikeyi, seeing evil everywhere! You, too, thus following the path trodden by wicked men, are making this bad resolution by ignorance."

verses.devanagari:
सत्यश्चाद्य प्रवादोऽयम् लौकिकः प्रतिभाति मा |
पित्ऱ्^ऊन् समनुजायन्ते नरा मातरमङ्गनाः
verses.iast:
satyaścādya pravādo'yam laukikaḥ pratibhāti mā |
pitR^ūn samanujāyante narā mātaramaṇ^ganāḥ
verses.translation: "The popular saying that males are born confirming to their fathers and females to their mothers, occurs to me as true."

verses.devanagari:
नैवम् भव ग़ृहाणेदम् यदाह वसुधाधिपः |
भर्तुरिच्चामुपास्वेह जनस्यास्य गतिर्भव
verses.iast:
naivam bhava Gṛhāṇedam yadāha vasudhādhipaḥ |
bharturiccāmupāsveha janasyāsya gatirbhava
verses.translation: Do not conform to the traits of your mother. Understand that which is said by the king. following the desire of your husband, be a protectress to these people here."

verses.devanagari:
मा त्वम् प्रोत्साहिता पापैर्देवराजसमप्रभम् |
भर्तारम् लोकभर्तारमसद्धर्ममुपादधाः
verses.iast:
mā tvam protsāhitā pāpairdevarājasamaprabham |
bhartāram lokabhartāramasaddharmamupādadhāḥ
verses.translation: "Incitedby the evil minded, do not put before the public an improper course of conduct of your husband who spendour is equal to that of king Devendra and who is a protector of this world.

glosses.meaning: do not put before the public
whose splendour is equal to the king Devendra
and who is a protector of this world.

verses.devanagari:
न हि मिथ्या प्रतिज्ञातम् करिष्यति तवानघः |
श्रीमान्दशरथो राजा देवि राजीवलोचनः
verses.iast:
na hi mithyā pratijJṇātam kariśhyati tavānaghaḥ |
śrīmāndaśaratho rājā devi rājīvalocanaḥ
verses.translation: "Oh, Kaikeyi! Dasaratha the faultless man, the majesty, the lotus-eyed man and the king cannot indeed belie the promise given to you(Hence, you alone has to change your opinion)"

verses.devanagari:
ज्येष्ठो वदान्यः कर्मण्यः स्वधर्मपरिरक्षिता |
रक्षिता जीवलोकस्य बली रामोऽभिषिच्यताम्
verses.iast:
jyeśhṭho vadānyaḥ karmaṇyaḥ svadharmaparirakśitā |
rakśitā jīvalokasya balī rāmo'bhiśhicyatām
verses.translation: "Let Rama the eldest(of the sons) who is generous strong skilled, capable of protecting his own duty as Kshatriya but also of protecting the world of living beings, be installed on the throne of Ayodhya"

glosses.meaning: the saviour of one's own righteousness
of the world of living being
be installed on the throne(of Ayodhya).

verses.devanagari:
परिवादो हि ते देवि महान्लोके चरिष्यति |
यदि रामो वनम् याति विहाय पितरम् नृपम्
verses.iast:
parivādo hi te devi mahānloke cariśhyati |
yadi rāmo vanam yāti vihāya pitaram nṛpam
verses.translation: "Oh, Kaikeyi! A great accusation will surely roam about you in the world, if Rama leaving his royal father goes to the forest.

verses.devanagari:
स राज्यम् राघवः पातु भवत्वम् विगतज्वरा |
न हि ते राघवादन्यः क्षमः पुरवरे वसेत्
verses.iast:
sa rājyam rāghavaḥ pātu bhavatvam vigatajvarā |
na hi te rāghavādanyaḥ kśamaḥ puravare vaset
verses.translation: "Let Rama of that character protect this kingdom! Be you free from distress. There is none other than Rama living in your excellent city who is competent to rule this Ayodhya"

verses.devanagari:
रामे हि यौवराज्यस्थे राजा दशरथो वनम् |
प्रवेक्ष्यति महेष्वासः पूर्ववृत्तमनुस्मरन्
verses.iast:
rāme hi yauvarājyasthe rājā daśaratho vanam |
pravekśyati maheśhvāsaḥ pūrvavṛttamanusmaran
verses.translation: "In the event of Rama being installe din the office of the prince Regent, King Dasaratha wielder of the great bow will surely have recourse to the forest, cherishly recollecting the conduct of his forebears"

glosses.meaning: being installed in the office of Price Regent
the wielder of the great bow

verses.devanagari:
इति सान्वैश्च तीक्ष्णै कैकेयीम् राजसंसदि |
सुवन्त्रः क्षोभयामास भूय एव कृताञ्जलिः
verses.iast:
iti sānvaiśca tīkśṇai kaikeyīm rājasaṃsadi |
suvantraḥ kśobhayāmāsa bhūya eva kṛtāJṇjaliḥ
verses.translation: Thus, Sumantra repeatedly with joint palms, caused a shaking to Kaikeyi in the royal assmebly, by his kind words as well as bitter words.

glosses.meaning: as well as his bitter words

verses.devanagari:
नैवसाक्षुभ्यते देवी न च स्म परिदूयते |
न चास्या मुखवर्णस्य विक्रिया लक्ष्यते तदा
verses.iast:
naivasākśubhyate devī na ca sma paridūyate |
na cāsyā mukhavarṇasya vikriyā lakśyate tadā
verses.translation: That queen Kaikeyi, however, was neither excited nor repented in her heart nor was any change observed in the colour of her face.

glosses.meaning: was not reapented in her heart
